insights.headline: Rupee at 96.31 and 5.34% US yields squeeze Indian buyers ahead of US payrolls
insights.summary: The rupee's slide to 96.31 — Asia's worst-performing currency on Thursday — is now the main price-setter for Indian bullion, keeping domestic gold and silver expensive in rupee terms. The 10-year US Treasury yield's rise to 5.34%, its highest since 2002, remains gold's biggest headwind, with Friday's US payrolls report deciding the Fed's next move. HSBC cut its 2026 average gold forecast to $4,490 but expects central banks to buy below $4,000; one technician sees a slide toward $3,920. With the festive season approaching, analysts say elevated prices may curb discretionary buying.
points: Rupee fell to 96.31 per dollar, its biggest single-day fall in over two months; FPIs have pulled about Rs 3 lakh crore from Indian equities in nine months.
US 10-year yield hit 5.34%, the highest since 2002; the dollar index rose to 101.90 and Brent crossed $100 a barrel.
September US payrolls due Friday at 1230 GMT; traders see only a ~25% chance of an October Fed hike.
HSBC cut its 2026 average gold forecast to $4,490/oz and 2027 to $4,825/oz, expecting central-bank buying to resume below $4,000.
MCX gold futures rose 0.67% to about Rs 1.47 lakh per 10 grams on Oct 1; silver gained 1% to Rs 2,25,934 per kg.

items.title: Rupee sinks to 96.31, logs biggest fall in over 2 months
items.summary: The rupee fell to 96.31 against the dollar on Friday, its sharpest single-day fall in over two months, as record foreign-investor selling — FPIs have pulled about Rs 3 lakh crore from Indian equities in nine months — combined with a surging dollar. With MCX fully closed for Gandhi Jayanti, a weaker rupee keeps imported gold and silver expensive in rupee terms even when global prices soften.

items.title: US Treasury yield hits the highest since 2002 at 5.34%
items.summary: The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield touched 5.34% on Thursday, its highest since 2002, as a global bond selloff swept markets. Higher yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold and drove bullion's roughly 6% September fall; Friday's US payrolls report (1230 GMT) is the next big input for Fed rate expectations.

items.title: HSBC lowers 2026 average gold price forecast to $4,490/oz
items.summary: HSBC cut its average gold price forecasts for 2026 and 2027 to $4,490 and $4,825 an ounce, saying bullion faces further near-term pressure but is likely approaching a bottom. The bank expects central banks to resume gold purchases as prices approach or fall below $4,000 an ounce.

items.title: MCX gold rises 0.67%, silver 1%; bullion rates also up on Oct 1
items.summary: MCX gold futures rose 0.67% to about Rs 1.47 lakh per 10 grams on October 1 and silver gained 1% to Rs 2,25,934 per kg, snapping a two-session slide as global cues firmed. In Delhi bullion markets, 24K gold was quoted near Rs 1,49,060 per 10 grams.

items.title: Gold shrugs off a 24-year high in bond yields while silver keeps sinking
items.summary: An analysis argues gold is defying decades of market history, holding near $4,180 even as the 10-year Treasury hit 5.34%, its highest since 2002. The reason: an estimated $840/oz 'de-dollarisation premium' from sustained central-bank buying (863 tonnes in 2025, per the World Gold Council). Silver, down 44-50% from its $121.62 January record after CME margin hikes, has no such structural buyer.

items.title: Gold alert: the USD index soars to new 2026 highs
items.summary: FXStreet analyst Przemyslaw Radomski argues gold's rebound to $4,251 on soft US inflation was sold the same afternoon — 'when a market fails to rally on news that should lift it, the buyers are not there' — and sees a head-and-shoulders breakdown targeting near $3,920. Silver settled at $60.57, its third straight lower close, as the dollar index hit new 2026 highs.

items.title: Should you invest in gold after the correction?
items.summary: With gold off about 6% in September, Outlook Money weighs the festive case: WGC data puts Indian household gold holdings near 31,000 tonnes (~$3.4 trillion); H1 2026 gold ETF demand rose 163% to 23.5 tonnes while jewellery demand fell 17% to 141.2 tonnes and bars/coins rose 21%. Peak festive demand could support prices, though elevated levels may curb discretionary buying.

items.title: Gold & silver price analysis: MCX bullion rebounds after sharp correction
items.summary: 24K gold held near Rs 1,49,570 per 10 grams (+0.52%) and MCX silver around Rs 2,26,190 per kg after the sharp correction, with physical demand resilient across metros on early festive-season buying. The piece flags the Fed's stance, oil prices and festive buying as the key drivers for bullion this week.

items.title: Asian shares tumble after wild swings in bonds, FX before US jobs data
items.summary: Asian equities fell on Friday as a bond-market rout and currency swings kept investors on edge before the September US payrolls report at 1230 GMT, the next big input for Fed rate expectations. The risk-off backdrop is one of the few supports for bullion amid record-high long-dated yields.

items.title: Rupee, bonds face pressure as US Treasury yields rise and crude tops $100
items.summary: The rupee fell 0.5% to 96.31 on Thursday — Asia's worst-performing currency — while India's 10-year bond yield rose to 7.21%, its highest since April 2024, as the US 10-year hit 5.34% and Brent crossed $100 a barrel. The rupee is down 6.68% in 2026 amid heavy FPI selling; dealers expect the 10-year gilt to touch 7.25% by the RBI's October 7 policy outcome.
